findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key is incompatible with datetime fields and crashes on any real use
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() (and value_from_cursor) are copied verbatim from the numeric Paginator implementation: `value = getattr(item, self.key); math.floor(value)`. But the endpoint wires this paginator up with `order_by="-datetime"` (organization_auditlogs.py), so `self.key` is "datetime" and `value` is a `datetime.datetime` instance. `math.floor()`/`math.ceil()` on a `datetime` object raises `TypeError` because datetime defines neither `__floor__` nor `__float__`. `build_cursor()` calls this key function on the first/last result as soon as there is at least one row, so any request to `/organization-audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true` made by an authorized admin that returns a non-empty result set will raise an unhandled exception (HTTP 500). The entire 'optimized pagination' feature is therefore non-functional for its only real caller.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch passes a negative start index into Django QuerySet slicing, which Django explicitly rejects
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative). Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for negative slice bounds; it does not 'properly handle negative slicing automatically' as the adjacent comment claims. As a result, the advertised 'negative offset support for efficient reverse pagination' will throw an unhandled exception any time it is exercised (e.g. a client-supplied cursor like `0:-5:0` combined with `optimized_pagination=true`), rather than providing any pagination benefit. The subsequent `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check also reuses the unclamped, possibly-negative `offset`, compounding the broken logic once/if the slicing issue is fixed.

findings.title: Unrelated behavioral change to shared BasePaginator.get_result() affects every consumer of Paginator/DateTimePaginator
findings.body: `BasePaginator.get_result()` is the shared implementation used by `Paginator` and `DateTimePaginator`, which are used by many unrelated list endpoints across the codebase, not just audit logs. This PR changes `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` to clamp the offset via `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, silently changing behavior for any caller that (intentionally or via a malformed cursor) passes a negative offset with `is_prev=False`: previously this would raise (Django disallows negative slice bounds), now it silently starts the page at 0. This is a meaningful behavior change to widely-shared pagination code, introduced only to support a feature that is itself broken (see other findings), with no test coverage and no changelog/documentation of the change. Additionally the accompanying comment says this 'allows negative offsets' when the code actually does the opposite (clamps negative offsets to zero in the non-prev branch), which will mislead future maintainers.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError if organization_context.member is None
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'` if `request.user.is_superuser` is False and `organization_context.member` is None (e.g. a non-superuser path that does not guarantee a member record, such as certain token-based or cross-silo access patterns). Other code in the codebase typically guards this with `organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access`. If this path is reachable, a normal GET request to this endpoint would 500 instead of falling back to standard pagination.

findings.title: No tests added for the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or the audit log endpoint's new pagination branch
findings.body: The PR introduces a new paginator class with a non-trivial negative-offset code path, a new `enable_advanced_features` flag, and a new permission-gated branch in `organization_auditlogs.py`, but no tests are included for any of it. Basic tests exercising `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` with real `AuditLogEntry` rows (ordered by `-datetime`) or the `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter against the endpoint would have immediately caught the `TypeError` in `get_item_key` and the `ValueError` from negative slicing described in other findings. Given the feature touches shared pagination infrastructure, the lack of coverage is a significant gap before merge.

findings.title: Misleading comments overstate Django's slicing capabilities and the safety of the feature
findings.body: The comments at lines 876 ('The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically') and 879 ('This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level') are factually incorrect/misleading: Django's QuerySet does not support negative slice bounds and will raise ValueError, and the 'safety' claim conflates authorization (who can call this code) with the actual boundary-condition correctness of slicing negative indices, which it is not. These comments will mislead future maintainers trying to understand or debug this code.

findings.title: Comment claims new 'advanced pagination' capability was added here, but no functional change was made
findings.body: The added comment states 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios... This enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets', but the line below it (`self.offset = int(offset)`) is unchanged from before the PR — `Cursor` already accepted negative integers via `int()`. The comment implies this file implements/enables a feature, when in fact the (broken) negative-offset handling lives entirely in paginator.py and is unrelated to this cast. This is misleading documentation that doesn't reflect any real change.

findings.title: New paginator duplicates ~65 lines of BasePaginator.get_result with no actual performance optimization
findings.body: Despite the PR's title and docstring claiming 'performance optimizations for high-traffic endpoints' and an 'optimized query path for large datasets', `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` is a near-verbatim copy-paste of `BasePaginator.get_result()` with one added (and broken, per other findings) branch for negative offsets. It performs the same queries, same hit counting, and same cursor-building as the base class — there is no demonstrated or plausible performance improvement. The duplication also means any future bug fix or improvement made to `BasePaginator.get_result()` will not automatically apply here, creating a maintenance hazard for logic that is already copy-pasted and partially incorrect.
